text.p: Sir Iain Vallance and Bert Roberts, the respective chairmen of British Telecommunications Plc(BT) and MCI Communications, will become co-chairmen of their merged company Concert, the firms said on Sunday.

BT's chief executive Sir Peter Bonfield, will become chief executive of the new company, while Gerald Taylor, president and chief executive officer of MCI will become president and ceo of Concert, but reporting to Bonfield.
Together, Bonfield and Taylor will comprise the office of the chief executive to which the senior management team of the huge combined group will report.
BT's group finance director Robert Brace and MCI's chief financial officer Doug Main will join the other four as executive board members, the statement added.

Alongside the executives, the board will also have nine non-executives. Sir Colin Marshall, non-executive deputy chairman of British Telecom, will remain deputy chairman of Concert and will be joined by eight other non-executives drawn equally from the boards of the two merging companies.
For Bonfield, a Briton whose career has included being chief executive and chairman of information technology group ICL, the merger marks a spectacular end to his first year as chief executive at BT.
He took over in January when the company split the roles of chairman and chief executive and Vallance, who had combined the roles since 1987, became chairman.
